t: Understanding Day-Count Conventions: Types and Uses in Finance
s: August 30, 2025 - Day-count conventions, including common types like 30/360 and actual/365, are essential in calculating accrued interest on financial instruments such as bonds and swaps. These methods standardize the process of determining the number of days between two dates, thus affecting interest calculations and present values.

In general the accrued interest will be equal to the number of days interest has accrued (in this case, ten) divided by the number of days in the coupon period times the future coupon payment (in this case, 6% of the face value, if the bond pays semiannually). It turns out that the amount of interest paid will depend on the kind of bond that you bought. Different types of bonds use different conventions for counting the time between two dates.
